title: MusicXML piano: pedal markers to SustainActive
description: Per [[musicxml-support]] Phase 8. bar.sustainPedals markers (Down/Hold/Up + ratioPosition) -> time-ordered pedal timeline per part; SustainActive = pedal down at note start. Markers sit only on the staff the <direction> attached to (usually bass), so apply part-wide to both hands. Handle <pedal type=change> per the survey.
notes:
Status 2026-10-03 (probe + ngd.1 survey of 2 musetrainer/library .mxl files). Determined (probe only): <pedal> -> bar.sustainPedals with pedalType Down/Hold/Up + ratioPosition, only on the staff the direction attached to. Not determined: everything real-file - neither surveyed file has pedal marks, so <pedal> vs <sound damper-pedal>, type=change, and staff attachment are unverified. Needs a real pedal sample before or during this bead.
Moved from ngd.1 (2026-10-04): real-file pedal check is part of this bead. Hand-author a pedal fixture (alphaTab <pedal> parsing confirmed by probe); try a real pedal sample if one turns up, otherwise ship against the fixture and fix-on-find for other exporters (<sound damper-pedal>).

title: MusicXML piano: note mapping (realValue, hands, tie merge)
description: Per [[musicxml-support]] Phase 8. Score beats -> SongKeyboardNote: Note=realValue (ottava already applied), timing via existing tick math, Hand from staff index (0=right, 1=left), middle-C split fallback for 1-staff or 3+-staff parts. Merge tie chains into one note with summed TimeLength (no Continued flag in SongKeyboardNote). Skip rests. Sections from masterBar.section like the guitar path.
notes:
Status 2026-10-03 (probe + ngd.1 survey of 2 musetrainer/library .mxl files). Determined: staff index = hand (real bass staff reaches A5, so not pitch); realValue = sounding pitch incl. ottava (probe only); ties surface as isTieDestination (43 in Twinkle); up to 3 voices/staff; grace notes steal ticks from the next beat (probe only). Not determined: ottava/grace in a real file; middle-C fallback behavior on 1-/3+-staff parts. Sections: masterBar.section empty for both real files (titles are <words>) - expect Sections: [] unless a file uses rehearsal marks.
Library source-of-truth survey 2026-10-09 (69 .mxl files, ~/Documents/RockyRoad/library/scores; staff count read from measure <attributes>, not part-list).

title: MusicXML piano: dynamics to Velocity, fix cross-staff dynamics leak
description: Per [[musicxml-support]] Phase 8. Map DynamicValue (PPP..FFF, default F) to 0-127 via a fixed table (decide values). alphaTab's _currentDynamics is part-wide and parse-ordered, so the bass staff inherits marks from later in the treble staff after <backup> (probe: p at t=0 -> bass reads f). Decide patch-package fix (upstream candidate, batch with ic6/msr) vs local workaround; pin with a fixture test.
notes:
Survey (ngd.1): leak runs both ways in real files (forward: Ode m.9 mf on staff 2; backward: Twinkle m.151 mid-bar f on staff 1 colors earlier bass beats). No per-staff rule recovers the timeline -> lean patch-package fix in _currentDynamics handling (upstream candidate). Table must cover FP/SFP/SFZ etc., not just PPP..FFF; hairpins = beat.crescendo only.
Status 2026-10-03 (probe + ngd.1 survey of 2 musetrainer/library .mxl files). Not determined: velocity table values (incl. FP/SFP/SFZ etc.); patch vs workaround (lean patch); whether hairpins (beat.crescendo) ramp velocity or are ignored; default F before first mark - keep or pick a quieter default.
Library source-of-truth survey 2026-10-09 (69 .mxl files, ~/Documents/RockyRoad/library/scores).
Cross-staff leak fixture: moonlight_sonata_3rd_movement.mxl - fp treble-only, pp bass-only, p/sf/f/f/ff on both staves, plus wedges (direction staff verified per-mark). Carol_of_the_Bells.mxl also splits (mp/mf staff 1, p staff 2, ff both). Bach_Toccata has f/mf/ff/p/mp on both.
fp/sfz-class for the accent table: fp in 12_Variations, Chopin Nocturne Eb, Sonate Moonlight 3rd, Pathetique 2nd (also rf), moonlight 3rd; sf/sfz in Beethoven Symphony 5 (sf+sfz), Arabesque (sf), Ballade (sf+fz), Entertainer_1902 (fz); sffz only in Hungarian_Dance_No_5.
Hairpins: nearly all files (both Moonlight 3rds, Hungarian, Carol, Twinkle variations, etc.).
Quiet opening / default velocity: 15 files have no dynamics at all - Prelude_I_BWV_846, Prelude_No_2_BWV_847, Lacrimosa_-_Requiem, G_Minor_Bach_Original, both Passacaglias, Bella_Ciao x2, Canon_easy, Carol_easy, Happy_Birthday_C_Major, Minuet_in_G_Major, Mozart_Allegro, Spring_Waltz_Mariage. Delayed first mark: Mariage_dAmour (m.11), Flight_of_the_Bumblebee (m.7), Air_on_G_String (m.6).

Started 2026-10-09 (Muse). Settled: velocity table mirrors alphaTab MidiUtils.dynamicToVelocity (min 15, step 16; F=95, p=47, ff=111, fff=127; SF/SFP/SFPP/SFZ/FZ/SFZP=111, FP/RF/RFZ/SFFZ=95, PF=87, N=1, PPPP/PPPPP/PPPPPP=10/5/3, FFFF+=127; RF group follows code not its stale FF comment); hairpins ignored (beat.crescendo has no target level); no-mark default stays F. Patch (not workaround): alphaTab already declares an unused per-staff StaffContext.currentDynamics - the fix wires all 5 _currentDynamics sites to it (direction + notations writes, 2 beat-creation reads, _createRestForGap gains a staff param). Pinned by fixtures/piano-dynamics-cross-staff.musicxml (both leak directions) + 3 single-staff mapping tests; full suite 64/64 + tsc clean. Upstream filing batches with ic6/msr per aio. Remaining before close: validate against a real library file (moonlight 3rd per-mark split) + ngd.6 wiring.
close_reason: Per-mark staff split verified on moonlight 3rd (both leak directions) + ngd.6 wiring landed; upstream filing stays with aio

title: MusicXML piano: detection + gate, grand-staff fixture
description: Per [[musicxml-support]] Phase 8. Scan non-stringed, non-percussion tracks independently of convertScore()'s fretted gate (like the lyrics scan). Rule: playbackInfo.program 1-7 -> piano; program 0 only with 2 staves or a name keyword (reuse pianoConverter.ts list) since missing <midi-program> also reads 0. Exclude detected piano parts from skipped. Add hand-authored grand-staff fixture (scratchpad probe file is a starting point).
notes:
Status 2026-10-03 (probe + ngd.1 survey of 2 musetrainer/library .mxl files). Determined: rule (program 1-7, or 0 + 2 staves/name keyword) catches both real files; missing <midi-program> also reads 0 (probe). Not determined: a real part with no <midi-program>; single-staff or 3+-staff keyboard parts; how non-piano 2-staff parts (harp, organ w/o program) behave under the rule.
Readiness 2026-10-04: unblocked (ngd.1 closed). Settle at start: (1) Detection order - stringed gate first, so a guitar part with no <midi-program> and std+tab staves (2 staves, program 0) is never mistaken for piano. (2) Keyword list: pianoConverter.ts uses substring includes('rh'/'lh'), which matches 'Rhythm'/'Lefty'; extract a shared helper and use word-boundary matching rather than copying it. (3) Result shape: detection lands in shared ScoreConvertResult (like lyrics), UI stays MusicXML-only; ngd.3 fills the notes. (4) Detected piano parts must not land in skipped (mirror the lyric-source exclusion in main.ts); a piano part that also carries lyrics feeds both consumers. (5) GP files with a single-staff piano track (program 0-7) will also be detected - confirm that's harmless since GP UI ignores it. Fixture: grand-staff, plus negative cases (guitar std+tab no program; 1-staff vocal; percussion).
Decision 2026-10-04: whole-word track-name matching, one shared helper used by determineRole (scoreConverter.ts), pianoConverter.ts, and the new piano detection. Tokenizer: strip dots (R.H. -> RH), split camelCase, split on non-letters (NBSP-safe, per the importer-NBSP lesson), match whole tokens against per-role alias lists. Probe of 34 names: whole-token fixes Bassoon/Rhythm->rh/Rhodes->rh/Lefty/Composer/Misleading; needs aliases for plural/suffix forms substring got by accident: bass(+contrabass), chord(chords), comp(comping), solo(soloist), piano(pianoforte, pno, keys); dotted R.H./L.H. need dot-stripping (fails under both today). Behavior change to existing guitar + MIDI paths - land as its own tested step with before/after cases; stringed bass already also keys off tuning range, so guitar regression risk is low.
Scope split (2026-10-04): in this bead - fretted-gate-first ordering, shared whole-word name helper (also applied to determineRole + pianoConverter), skipped-list exclusion, result shape, GP single-staff check, fixtures + negative cases, 2-staff non-piano rule documented. Deferred: hand-split fallback for 1-/3+-staff parts -> ngd.3; no-<midi-program> real part -> fix-on-find; pedal/dynamics/repeats/title -> ngd.4/.5/.6/3sp.
close_reason: Detection + gate-first ordering + shared whole-word name helper + grand-staff fixture and negative cases, 52 vitest green, tsc clean. Note mapping deferred to ngd.3.

title: MusicXML: multi-staff guitar tracks silently skipped (checks staves[0] only)
description: Per [[musicxml-support]]: convertScore() (SongConverter/src/scoreConverter.ts ~L216) only inspects track.staves[0] to decide if a track is fretted (!staff.isStringed -> skipped.push). Real TuxGuitar 2.1 export (/home/andrew/Music/MusicXML/the-beatles-let_it_be.musicxml) puts standard notation on staff 0 (no tuning, isStringed=false) and the actual tab data on staff 1 (TAB clef, isStringed=true, tuning=[64,59,55,50,45,40]). Result: the only guitar track in a real-world file is pushed entirely into skipped and never converted - not a technique-fidelity gap, a total miss. Confirmed via a throwaway probe test (not committed) running convertMusicXml against the real file; per-track dump showed staff[0].isStringed=false / staff[1].isStringed=true,tuning populated. Fix: scan all of track.staves for one with isStringed (prefer the one with showTablature, matching how TuxGuitar/MuseScore structure multi-staff tab exports) instead of assuming index 0. Blocks real end-to-end validation of ic6's hammer-on/pull-off fix and other Phase 1/5 behaviors against this file.
close_reason: Fixed: convertScore() now scans all of track.staves for one with isStringed (not staff.isPercussion) instead of assuming index 0. Verified against the real TuxGuitar 2.1 export: Guitar track now converts (was fully skipped before), 134 notes, HammerOn=3/PullOff=3 correctly linked (matches source markup, also validates ic6's patch-package fix against real-world data), tuning correctly read as standard EADGBE (all-zero offsets). tsc clean, all 25 existing tests still pass unaffected.

title: MusicXML: add Score-side vocals consumer (beats to SongVocal, source select, vocals.json)
description:
Per [[musicxml-support]] lyrics section and RockyRoadImport-msr: the
syllabic patch has no Score-side consumer. OpenSongChart supports vocals
and the PSARC path emits them (PsarcConverter.cs vocals branch +
ChartUtil.FormatVocals, written out via main.ts `part.Notes ?? part.Vocals`),
but `scoreConverter.ts` / the MusicXML tab handle notes only.

Verified ground truth (installed @coderline/alphatab@1.8.4 dist):
- `beat.lyrics` is `string[] | null`, indexed per verse line by `<lyric number>`
  (via getLyricLine map). `_parseLyric` switches on `<text>`/`<elision>` only;
  `syllabic` appears nowhere. Repeated `<text>` within one entry space-joins.
- `SongVocal { Vocal: string, TimeOffset: number }` has no continues-word flag,
  so begin/middle/end runs must merge into single entries at conversion time.
- Timing reuses the existing tick math:
  `ticksToSeconds(beat.absolutePlaybackStart, tempoMap, division)`.
- A vocal-only part is non-stringed, so `convertScore()`'s current gate would
  drop it into `skipped` — the consumer must scan lyric-bearing tracks
  independently of the fretted-instrument gate, not just post-process kept tracks.

Scope:
- Extract in `scoreConverter.ts` as a new result field (e.g. per-track lyric
  runs), package in the MusicXML tab as `vocals.json` plus a vocals
  `SongInstrumentPart` (`InstrumentName: 'vocals'`, `InstrumentType: 'Vocals'`)
  in song.json `InstrumentParts`, and fold vocal times into SongLengthSeconds.
- Lyric-source select per the 0fx decision (unbuilt): auto-pick when exactly one
  part carries lyric data, else a `<select>` in `musicxml-metadata-form`
  (main.ts) listing those track names, defaulting to the first.
- Verse choice is open: `beat.lyrics` can carry several lines; default to line 0
  unless a file shows otherwise.
- `FormatVocals` (C# 40-char syllable-aware wrap) has no TS equivalent on the
  Score path — decide port vs skip. Rocksmith's `+` line-break convention has no
  MusicXML analog either (extenders/melisma unhandled); document, don't invent.
- Decide whether the GP tab gets the same consumer (GP tracks can carry lyrics
  via applyLyrics) or MusicXML-only for v1.
- Ordering: build the plain-text consumer first (needs no patch); the
  begin/middle/end join lands on top once msr's patch exists. Until then,
  multi-syllable words come through as separate entries — surface as a known
  limit in the status line alongside the existing slap/pop/harmonic suffix.
- Tests follow the Phase 6 pattern: small hand-authored fixtures (one lyric part;
  two lyric parts for the auto-pick/select case). A syllabic-join test waits on msr.
close_reason: Vocals consumer built, 36/36 + tsc clean, log filed

comments.author: Andrew Gwinner
comments.text:
Build-readiness review (2026-10-03): checked the bead against scoreConverter.ts, main.ts MusicXML tab, PsarcConverter.cs/ChartUtil.cs, the installed alphaTab dist, and the MusicXML lyric spec. Most gaps resolve to an existing pattern or verified fact:

- Patch is live at runtime: alphaTab.mjs is a 4KB shim over the patched alphaTab.core.mjs (syllabic test passes). Only CJS/vite/webpack/min bundles are unpatched, so keep the Array.isArray(beat.lyricsSyllabic) guard and let the existing test trip if the patch is ever lost.
- Verse default: getLyricLine maps any number string first-seen-first-indexed, so "line 0" already means first verse seen. No verse UI for v1.
- Beat eligibility: mirror applyLyrics — skip isEmpty/isRest beats and "" entries.
- Vocals-only gate: main.ts early-returns on tracks.length === 0, blocking vocals-only files. New gate: tracks.length === 0 && !vocals. Exclude the selected lyric track from skipped so the status line doesn't misreport it.
- Output contract: follow the existing ${InstrumentName}.json pattern with InstrumentName 'vocals' / InstrumentType 'Vocals' (vocals.json falls out free, same as psarc path). SongLengthSeconds extends the existing reduce with max(vocal TimeOffset), documented as onset-only approximation.
- FormatVocals: port, don't skip (~30 lines in ChartUtil.cs plus the '+' -> '\n' step in PsarcConverter.cs:143). Keeps renderer parity with the psarc path; directly unit-testable.
- Word-join: concatenate begin/(middle)*/end runs with no separator, TimeOffset of run start; degraded runs pass through as-is. <extend>/melisma stays a documented limit.
- Source select: add a "Lyrics from" row to musicxml-metadata-form, populated on parse, hidden on 0-1 lyric tracks; status line gains Lyrics: <track>. plus the vocals caveat on the known-limits suffix.
- GP scope: v1 MusicXML-only, but place the consumer in shared convertScore() output so GP parity stays open at zero rework cost.

Genuinely remaining: downstream renderer acceptance of vocals-only songs (outside this repo); verse-select UI and GP parity deferred until a real file needs them.

comments.author: Andrew Gwinner
comments.text:
Implemented (uncommitted, on feat/MusicXML): Score-side vocals consumer per the build-readiness comment.

- SongConverter/src/vocals.ts (new): extractTrackLyrics (all-staff scan, verse 0, tick+text dedupe, rest/empty skip), mergeLyricEntries (begin/middle/end join, graceful strays), formatVocals (ChartUtil port, no '+' rewrite — MusicXML '+' stays literal).
- scoreConverter.ts: ScoreConvertResult.lyrics populated for every Score (GP path ignores it; v1 UI is MusicXML-only).
- main.ts MusicXML tab: vocals-only files pass the gate, single lyric part auto-picks, multi-part gets a <select> in the metadata form, lyric source excluded from skipped, vocals.json + vocals InstrumentPart + length fold-in on download, status reports lyric source and the syllabic caveat only when the patch signal is absent.
- SongConverter/src/vocals.test.ts (new, 8 tests): merge/format units plus hand-authored lyric fixtures (single, two-part, lyric-free). Full suite 36/36, tsc clean.

One new gotcha (not lesson-filed — quick diagnosis, no product impact): alphaTab normalizes spaces in track names to U+00A0, so assertions against multi-word part names fail invisibly. Fixtures use single-word names; the UI select is self-consistent since it reuses the same strings.

title: MusicXML: patch alphaTab to surface <syllabic> for lyric word-joining (mirror ic6)
description:
Per [[musicxml-support]] lyrics section: alphaTab's MusicXmlImporter._parseLyric (confirmed in installed @coderline/alphatab@1.8.4 dist) only switches on <text>/<elision> child elements - <syllabic> (single/begin/middle/end) is never referenced anywhere in the function, not even a no-op case branch. Same silent-drop class as harmonic, but recoverable the same way Phase 2's hammer-on/pull-off bug was: a local patch-package patch, verified against our own test suite, then written up as a fork + upstream PR against CoderLine/alphaTab (same workflow already underway for ic6's noteStringLookup fix - explore doing it the same way here).

Contract with the Score-side consumer (RockyRoadImport-m2g, the follow-up bead): m2g owns the beats-to-SongVocal walk (selected verse line of the selected track, existing tick math for timing) and the run-merge. So this bead takes the parallel-signal shape, not join-at-parse: surface per-entry syllabic values alongside beat.lyrics (e.g. a beat.lyricsSyllabic array with the same per-verse indexing), and leave joining to m2g's consumer. One merge site then serves both the patched path and the no-patch fallback (separate entries, surfaced as a known limit); verse and source-select logic stay in the consumer instead of being split across the patch.

SongVocal{Vocal,TimeOffset} has no field for 'continues previous word', so m2g's code merges begin/middle/end runs into a single SongVocal entry at conversion time regardless - the schema has nowhere else to carry that signal.

Verification split: patch unit-verified at the alphaTab level (parse yields surfaced syllabic values; no regression on text/elision space-joining); end-to-end word-join rides on m2g's consumer once both land. Upstream filing batches with ic6's held filing (alphaTab requires issue-before-PR plus AI-disclosure block).
notes: Fork-side fix prepared 2026-10-03 in /home/andrew/Documents/RockyRoad/alphaTab, branch fix/musicxml-lyric-syllabic (commit 3507d05e): TS-source Beat.lyricsSyllabic + _parseLyric case (replacing the 'not supported' comment), regenerated cloner/serializer, lyric-syllabic.xml fixture + unit test with JSON round-trip (fails pre, passes post; importer file 29/29, model 163/163, tsc/biome clean). No visual reference test: render output is byte-identical. Upstream issue/PR still deferred to batch with ic6 per its close note.

comments.author: Andrew Gwinner
comments.text:
Decided 2026-10-01 (lyrics source selection): auto-pick the track's lyrics when exactly
one part carries non-empty beat.lyrics (the common case, no UI shown). When >1 part has
lyric data (duet/backing-vocal/dual-purpose-track files), show a <select> in the existing
musicxml-metadata-form (main.ts) listing those track names, defaulting to the first -
mirrors the project's existing surface-ambiguity-don't-guess pattern (status-line
skipped-track/known-limits reporting) rather than a naming heuristic that breaks on
duets/choirs.

Still open (multi-syllable words, <lyric><syllabic>): not just a "document it" item -
alphaTab's importer drops <syllabic> entirely (confirmed no-op, same category as harmonic),
so there's no data to read even if we wanted higher fidelity. Real sub-decisions if this
is ever revisited past v1:
  1. Scope: stay with the documented-limitation treatment (separate lyric entries, no
     word-joining - current lean, consistent with slap/pop/harmonic precedent) vs. invest
     in recovering fidelity.
  2. If recovering fidelity: patch alphaTab to surface syllabic (patch-package, same
     category as the Phase 2 noteStringLookup fix) vs. bypass alphaTab's object model for
     this one field and do an independent lightweight scan of the raw <lyric> elements
     ourselves.
  3. Output mapping: SongVocal has no field for "continues previous word" - recovering
     fidelity means merging begin/middle/end runs into one joined Vocal string at
     conversion time, not just tagging entries, since the schema has nowhere else to put it.
Leaning: not worth it for v1 - narrow gap, no schema slot ready for it, and the recovery
paths are comparable effort to Phase 2's harder fixes for a smaller payoff.
